request.spec:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures in the header now show, for each grade, the due-totals of non-retired people on that grade added up across the sheet tree. They also show, for each status, how many claims across the tree have that status. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The whole change is in one file, `src/main/frontend/features/header/consolidated.slot.tsx`. The screen already worked out the consolidated figures one sheet at a time, and I added the new figures to that same pass:

- **Per grade:** each person is placed by their grade on their own sheet's today, and their due-total is the one their person row shows. That is the same rule the existing summary's per-grade total uses. The totals skip n/a values and appear as `consolidated-grade-{A,B,C}-due-total`.
- **Per status:** each sheet's claims are counted per status, the same way the summary counts them, and the counts are added up across the tree. They appear as `consolidated-status-{DRAFT,OPEN,PENDING,SETTLED,VOID,REVIEW}-count`.

Everything is computed in the browser, so the stored data, the server and the audit file are unchanged. The new figures follow the screen's as-of date, as the existing consolidated figures do.
